title: Practical Feasibility of the SAT-Solver Attack on Sprout
summary: The stated estimate exceeds a work factor of two to the eightieth when e is above 23, but the SAT-solver attack's feasibility against full Sprout remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the SAT-solver attack previously given for Sprout constitutes a feasible practical attack on full Sprout under its stated complexity assumptions. The attack is described as requiring $2^{54}$ attempts, with each attempt costing approximately $6.6 \cdot 2^{54} \cdot 2^e$ Sprout encryptions; this exceeds $2^{80}$ work when $e>23$. The unresolved task is to establish, either analytically or through practical experimentation, whether the attack can be carried out feasibly against full Sprout under those parameters and assumptions.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptanalysis and practical SAT-solver attack evaluation for the Sprout stream cipher.
assumptions: The prior attack's reported complexity model is used to assess practical feasibility.
parameters: $2^{54}$ attempts — stated number of SAT-solver attack attempts
$6.6 \cdot 2^{54} \cdot 2^e$ Sprout encryptions — approximate cost per attempt
$e$ — exponent governing the per-attempt cost, with the stated work exceeding $2^{80}$ when $e>23$
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish analytically or experimentally whether the attack can be carried out feasibly against full Sprout under the stated parameters and assumptions.

citations.label: Another Tradeoff Attack on Sprout-Like Stream Ciphers

progress.summary: The source summarizes the prior SAT-solver attack's complexity and explicitly questions whether it translates into a feasible attack on Sprout. It leaves that feasibility question unresolved.
